private List<BuildingRegistration> GetSupervisedStores()
{
    if (_supervisedStoresCacheFrame == Time.frameCount)
        return _supervisedStoresCache;
    _supervisedStoresCacheFrame = Time.frameCount;
    _supervisedStoresCache = new List<BuildingRegistration>();
    foreach (BuildingRegistration buildingRegistration in SaveGameManager.Current.BuildingRegistrations)
    {
        if (IsSupervisedStore(buildingRegistration))
            _supervisedStoresCache.Add(buildingRegistration);
    }
    return _supervisedStoresCache;
}
private bool IsSupervisedStore(BuildingRegistration registration)
{
    if (PricingManagerHelper.IsManageableBusiness(registration))
        return registration.Neighborhood == supervisedNeighborhood;
    return false;
}

============================================================
3. CLOSEST STRUCTURAL TEMPLATE FOR "STORE MANAGER SUPERVISES N STORES"
============================================================
Use a HYBRID of two existing shapes; the PricingManager neighborhood model is the WRONG shape (supervise-a-whole-neighborhood, uncapped) but its filter predicate is right.

(a) Count-capped explicit list — from HrManagerPlan: `assignedEmployees : List<string>` + `MaxEmployees` from skill (`10 + floor(skill/25)*10`) + reverse pointer `EmployeeInstance.assignedHrManagerPlanId`. This is the ONLY native plan that supervises "N discrete entities capped by manager skill". For the Store Manager: `assignedStores : List<Address>` (or building-id strings) + `MaxStores` computed identically (tune constants), enforced in the mod's own UI like `HrManagerPlanUI.CanAssignMore`/`Fill()`.
(b) Per-target rich sub-object — from LogisticsManagerPlan.destinations: `List<LogisticsManagerPlanDestination>` where each = `{ Address deliveryTargetAddress; List<ItemAmountTarget> stockTargets; }`. This is exactly the StoreManagerMod "per-store limits + weekly restock targets". Model each supervised store as `{ Address store; List<ItemAmountTarget> restockTargets; ... }`. The weekly restock itself already uses `GameInstance.DeliveryContracts` (store DeliveryContract), analogous to how LogisticsManagerPlanDestination.Deliver tops up store stock.
(c) Store eligibility filter — reuse `PricingManagerHelper.IsManageableBusiness(reg)` verbatim (RentedByPlayer + `retailPrices != null` + BusinessType has `generatesrevenue` tag). Iterate `SaveGameManager.Current.BuildingRegistrations` exactly like `GetSupervisedStores()` above, but filter by "id ∈ assignedStores" rather than "Neighborhood == supervisedNeighborhood".

For the Team Leader (department tier): the game has NO shelf-grouping / department entity. Closest primitives: `PricingManagerPlan.manuallyPricedItems : HashSet<string>` and `LogisticsManagerPlanDestination.stockTargets` are both keyed by item name; product universe of a store comes from `BusinessTypeHelper.GetAllProducts(businessTypeName)` + `store.cachedAvailableProducts` (see `PricingManagerPlan.GetSellableItems` L411-430). So a "department" is mod-invented = a named `HashSet<string>` of product categories / item-name sets within one store; the Team Leader plan holds `{ Address store; string departmentName; HashSet<string> productNames; List<ItemAmountTarget> requestedTargets }`, and the Store Manager plan references Team-Leader-plan ids the way `HeadhunterPlan.assignedHrPlans` references Hr-plan ids.

4. PLAN-LIST UI CLASSES (template for the mod HQ tab content)
============================================================
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HRManagers.HrManagersPlanList` — …/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers/HrManagersPlanList.cs
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PricingManagers.PricingManagersPlanList` — …/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PricingManagers/PricingManagersPlanList.cs
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.LogisticsManagers.LogisticsManagersPlanList` — …/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.LogisticsManagers/LogisticsManagersPlanList.cs
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.PurchasingAgentsPlanList` — …/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/PurchasingAgentsPlanList.cs
All are `MonoBehaviour` with heavy `[SerializeField]` prefab refs: `entryTemplate` (Transform or a typed `*PlanListEntry`), `buttonEntry` (the "+" add row), `reorderableList : ReorderableList`, a detail panel (`*PlanUI`), and a `NoManagerAssignedPopUp`. Render pattern (`RefreshPlansList` / `SetUpPlanEntry`):
  1. `entryTemplate.(transform.)ResetTemplate()` (hide template, destroy clones).
  2. `foreach plan in <Helper>.GetAssignedPlansForHeadquarters(bizMan.business.address)` → `Object.Instantiate(entryTemplate, entryTemplate.parent)`; wire `Button.onClick → SelectPlan(plan)`; set labels via extension helpers `entry.GetLabelByName("ManagerName")`, `"Info"` = `$"{plan.NumberOfAssignedEmployees}/{plan.MaxEmployees}"`; populate a manager `UI.Elements.Dropdown` from `entry.GetDropDownByName("ManagerDropdown")` with `common_unassigned` + eligible employees (predicate: `x.assignedAddress == HQ.address && x.HasSkill(skill) && !assignedToOtherPlan(x.id) && x.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()`).
  3. `buttonEntry.SetAsLastSibling(); reorderableList.Reinitialize();`
  4. `AddPlan()` → `new <Plan>{ headquartersAddress = InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.fullMenu.bizMan.business.address }` → add to `SaveGameManager.Current.<list>` (or `<Helper>.AddPlan`) → `SetUpPlanEntry` → `SelectPlan` → `SaveGameManager.MarkChange()`.
  5. Reorder callback writes directly into `SaveGameManager.Current.<list>` (`UpdatePlanOrder` / `OnPlanReordered`).
Every entry row and detail panel is a baked prefab inside the game's addressables. A mod tab therefore either ships an AssetBundle of cloned prefabs, or hand-builds pure-UGUI GameObjects at runtime (no Radzen here — this is Unity uGUI), e.g. via ModOptions `AddCustom(SpawnUi)` or Harmony-injected GameObjects.

============================================================
5. HQ TAB IS HARD-CODED (template for adding the mod tab)
============================================================
`BizManBusiness` — …/BizManBusiness.cs (MonoBehaviour). `[SerializeField] Transform menu; [SerializeField] Transform containers;` (L36-39).
`SetUpTabs()` (L203-253): builds private `List<string> _tabs` via literal switch on `buildingRegistration.businessTypeName`. For `"ba:businesstype_headquarters"` (L222-231) it adds exactly: `Schedule, PricingManagers, LogisticsManagers, PurchasingAgents, HRManagers, Headhunters, Settings`. Then `foreach Transform in menu: item.gameObject.SetActive(_tabs.Contains(item.name));`.
`Awake()` (L118-144): `foreach Transform tab in menu.transform` wires `tab.GetComponent<Button>().onClick → SetTab(tab.name)`.
`SetTab(tabName)` (L294-344): `containers.Find(tabName)` toggles the container GameObject; per-tab `switch` runs a refresh (Insight/InventoryPricing/Schedule/Settings/Marketing).
`SetInitialTab()` (L255-292): hardcodes HQ → `_selectedTab = "PricingManagers"`.
So a mod tab needs: (i) Harmony postfix on `SetUpTabs` to append the mod tab name to `_tabs` when HQ; (ii) a new tab-label GameObject parented under `menu`, named identically, with a Button whose onClick calls SetTab (add via Harmony on `Awake` or manually after open); (iii) a matching content GameObject parented under `containers` with the same name, hosting the mod's plan-list MonoBehaviour; (iv) optionally a `SetTab` prefix/postfix if the tab needs a refresh hook.

============================================================
6. SAVE-SYSTEM COMPAT PASSES THAT PURGE PLANS
============================================================
Runner: `SaveGameCompatibilityFixes.ApplyCompatibilityFixes(gameInstance)` (…/Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes/SaveGameCompatibilityFixes.cs) runs on EVERY load: first `CompatibilityItemValidator.ValidateGameInstance` (unconditional), then 11 `ICompatibilityVersion` entries (`UpdateGameInstanceToEA02..EA011`, `UpdateGameInstanceTo1`), each `RunPriority` then `Run`.
GATE: `ICompatibilityVersion` (…/ICompatibilityVersion.cs L37 & L59) only invokes `fix.Apply(gameInstance)` when `gameInstance.buildNumberAtLastSave <= item.buildNumber`. A save last written by build 3672 therefore SKIPS every purge shipped so far — but any future game update can register a new `(fix, <newBuild>)` tuple which then fires against essentially every pre-existing save on first load after the update.

Plan-purging fixes:
- `RemoveInvalidPlans` — …/Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes.CompatibilityFixesEA010/RemoveInvalidPlans.cs (registered at build 3452, "before loading", in UpdateGameInstanceToEA010.cs L33). For `logisticsManagerPlans`, `headhunterPlans`, `hrManagerPlans`, `importPartnerships`, `DeliveryContracts`: if `headquartersAddress` (logistics also `targetAddress`) resolves to a `BuildingRegistration` with `!RentedByPlayer`, calls `CompatibilityHelper.Remove<Type>Plan(address)` which deletes ALL plans of that type at that address. Also: for every `EmployeeInstance`, if `assignedHrManagerPlanId` matches no surviving plan → null it.
- `RemoveOrphanedPricingManagerPlans` — …/Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes.CompatibilityFixes1/RemoveOrphanedPricingManagerPlans.cs (registered at build 3655 in UpdateGameInstanceTo1.cs L24). Removes any `pricingManagerPlans[i]` whose `headquartersAddress` building is `!RentedByPlayer`.
- `UpdateLogisticsManagerPlans` — CompatibilityFixesEA010 (3422, "after loading"): re-derives `isFactory`, and for factory plans `destinations.RemoveAll` where the destination is not a warehouse/importexport.
- `RemoveLegacyFactoryItemsFromLogisticPlans` (EA010, 3447) and `RemoveNonQuantityItemsFromLogisticsManagerPlans` (EA06): strip `stockTargets` whose item is not `ItemType.RetailProduct` (except paperbag).
- `UpdateHeadquartersPlansToNewSystem` — …/Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes.CompatibilityFixesEA06/UpdateHeadquartersPlansToNewSystem.cs: one-time migration that OUTRIGHT REPLACED `gameInstance.logisticsManagerPlans / headhunterPlans / hrManagerPlans` with `new List<...>()` and rebuilt them from now-`[Obsolete]` per-EmployeeInstance fields (HRManager.assignedEmployees, LogisticsManager.deliveryPlans, etc.). Precedent that the devs will wholesale-rewrite these lists across a version.
- `InitializePricingManagerPlans` — CompatibilityFixesEA011: `if (pricingManagerPlans == null) pricingManagerPlans = new()`.
- `CompatibilityItemValidator.ValidateImportPartnerships` (…/Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes/CompatibilityItemValidator.cs L44-66, UNCONDITIONAL every load): removes `ImportProduct`s whose `itemName` cannot be resolved by `ItemsGetter.GetByName`. It does NOT touch `modData`.

Runtime (non-compat) purges — fire whenever the player closes / sells / transfers a building:
- `BusinessHelper.DeleteHQPlans(registration)` — …/Helpers/BusinessHelper.cs L984-1010: deletes every `importPartnerships` / `logisticsManagerPlans` / `headhunterPlans` / `hrManagerPlans` / `pricingManagerPlans` whose `headquartersAddress == registration.Address`. Called from `BusinessHelper.ShutdownBusiness` (L932), `BizManSettings` L209 (close-business), `BizManTransfer` L64, and compat `DeleteHiddenPlansFromNonHQBusinesses`.
- `BusinessHelper.ShutdownBusiness` (L927) also calls `LogisticsManagerHelper.ShutdownBusiness` / `CancelAllDeliveriesForAddress`, and `PurchasingAgentHelper.CancelPlansThatDeliverToAddress` for warehouses.
- `CompatibilityHelper.RemoveHqPlans(address)` — …/Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes/CompatibilityHelper.cs L218-226: same wipe during building-eviction migrations.

============================================================
7. WHY THE MOD CANNOT ADD A REAL NEW PLAN TYPE TO GameInstance — MUST USE modData
============================================================
1. `GameInstance` is a non-partial `public class` compiled into BigAmbitions.dll (GameInstance.cs L24). The mod is a separate, later-loaded assembly; C# cannot add instance fields to an already-compiled type, and Harmony patches methods, not fields.
2. Serialization is closed. `SaveGameSerializationHelper` (…/SaveGameSerializationHelper.cs) serializes `GameInstance` BY VALUE via OdinSerializer binary (`SerializationUtility.SerializeValue(instance, stream, DataFormat.Binary, SerializationContext)` with a fixed `SaveGameSerializationPolicy`, L58-80) or Newtonsoft (`JsonConvert.SerializeObject(instance, …)`, L42-56). Both walk the concrete members of `GameInstance` as declared in the game assembly. A field that does not exist on the type is never written; on load Newtonsoft silently drops unknown JSON and Odin (`AllowDeserializeInvalidData = true`, L240) discards unknown entries. A mod "plan list" cannot round-trip even if you could attach one.
3. A Harmony side-channel (static `ConditionalWeakTable<GameInstance, ModState>` + patches on save/load) still needs a real persistence sink, and the ONLY mod-writable serialized member is `GameInstance.modData : Dictionary<string,string>` (L248) — Odin/Newtonsoft do serialize it, and it is already proven in the reflection dump (another mod uses it). `GlobalEvents.onSaveGame` (…/GlobalEvents.cs L28) is a `public static Action` that fires synchronously before serialize — the mod flushes its plan as a JSON string into `modData` there and re-hydrates on load / `GlobalEvents.RegisterOnGameLoadedCallback`.
4. Being "real" buys nothing at runtime: `GameManager.RunMainGameTick` / `NewDay` call a hard-coded set of helpers (`PricingManagerHelper.RunHourly` L592, `LogisticsManagerHelper.DoAll*Deliveries` L601/610, `ImportPartnership.DoAllDeliveries` L606, `EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily` L649). Nothing generic iterates "all plan lists". A mod plan gets NO engine callback regardless of storage — it must run its own tick from `GlobalEvents.onNewDay` / `onNewHour` (…/GlobalEvents.cs L16/L18), doing its own manager lookup (`EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeById`, `IsEmployeeAvailable`) exactly as the native helpers do.
5. Being "real" actively HURTS: the compat framework and `BusinessHelper.DeleteHQPlans` enumerate the KNOWN lists; a future `RemoveOrphaned*` / `RemoveInvalidPlans`-style fix (gated only by `buildNumberAtLastSave <= newBuild`, which every existing save satisfies at update time) could silently wipe unrecognised data, and precedent (`UpdateHeadquartersPlansToNewSystem`) shows the devs will `new List<>()` these outright. `modData` is opaque to all of it — no `ICompatibilityFix` and no `CompatibilityItemValidator` path touches `modData` — so the mod owns its own GC: mirror `RemoveInvalidPlans` by dropping supervised-store entries whose `BuildingRegistration` is gone or `!RentedByPlayer`, and mirror `ValidateImportPartnerships` by dropping `ItemAmountTarget`s that fail `ItemsGetter.GetByName`.

keyTypes.name: PricingManagerPlan

keyTypes.name: LogisticsManagerPlan

keyTypes.name: LogisticsManagerHelper

GetEmployeeById, EmployeeInstancesDictionary, CreateAIEmployeeInstance, HireCandidate, CalculateHourlyWageForSkill.

keyTypes.name: CompatibilityItemValidator
keyTypes.note: ValidateGameInstance runs unconditionally every load. ValidateImportPartnerships L44-66 removes ImportProducts with unresolvable item names. Does NOT touch modData — mod must validate its own item-name targets.

keyTypes.name: SaveGameSerializationHelper
keyTypes.note: Serializes GameInstance by value: OdinSerializer binary (SerializeValue, fixed SaveGameSerializationPolicy, L58-80) or Newtonsoft (L42). Walks concrete members of the compiled type; unknown fields never written, unknown data discarded on load (AllowDeserializeInvalidData L240).

keyTypes.name: RecruitmentHelper
keyTypes.note: GenerateCandidate L41-85: switch on skillName → LogisticsManager/HRManager/Headhunter/PricingManager, else plain EmployeeInstance. Adds primary skill + SkillData.secondarySkill, sets hourlyWage via CalculateHourlyWageForSkill, adds to Current.CandidateEmployeeInstances. Template for spawning the two new-role candidates.

feasibility: Needs Harmony + prefab-less runtime UI (or a shipped AssetBundle) for the HQ BizMan tab; plan state MUST live in GameInstance.modData (JSON string) with a mod-run driver on GlobalEvents.onNewDay/onNewHour and flush on GlobalEvents.onSaveGame. A native GameInstance plan list is IMPOSSIBLE for a mod (GameInstance is a non-partial compiled class; OdinSerializer/Newtonsoft serialize it by value; nothing in the engine tick loop would call a mod plan anyway; and the compat framework + BusinessHelper.DeleteHQPlans would be a liability, not a benefit). The supervision LOGIC ports cleanly: reuse HrManagerPlan's capped-explicit-list shape (assignedStores List<Address> + MaxStores from skill via a 10+floor(skill/25)*10-style formula + a mod-side reverse index) combined with LogisticsManagerPlanDestination's {address + List<ItemAmountTarget>} per-store restock-target sub-object, and PricingManagerHelper.IsManageableBusiness as the store-eligibility filter. Tier hierarchy (Team Leader → Store Manager) can copy HeadhunterPlan.assignedHrPlans (a plan referencing other plans' ids). Departments have no game concept — model as a mod-invented named HashSet<string> of product/item names within one store (primitives: BusinessTypeHelper.GetAllProducts + store.cachedAvailableProducts). Risk is concentrated in: (a) the hard-coded BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs/Awake/SetTab needing Harmony + hand-built menu/containers GameObjects, (b) strict modData round-trip discipline, (c) the mod owning its own orphan-GC (mirror RemoveInvalidPlans + ValidateImportPartnerships) because no compat pass will maintain modData.
openQuestions: HQ 'capacity' / 'expand HQ': there is NO Headquarters building class or manager-slot cap in the Buildings.Office.Headquarters namespace (it holds only plan helpers). How many managers an HQ holds is implicitly bounded by employee-station/desk items at the HQ address + work-shift assignment. Need to confirm whether 'expand the HQ' means renting a larger HQ building / placing more desk items, and whether any BusinessType data or business-requirement gates HQ headcount.

The Purchasing Agent HQ tab (PurchasingAgentsPlanList) has NO 'add plan' button — ImportPartnerships are created via ImportManagerDialog / the importer's contact. If the two new roles must be 'hired at the same place as the Purchasing Agent', clarify whether that means the Recruitment Agency (candidate generation) or the HQ tab, and whether the mod plan is created from an HQ '+' button (HR/Pricing/Logistics style) or from a dialog.

Custom-skill lifecycle for the two new skills (SkillHelper.GetData is unguarded in ~8 hot paths; skills re-register per city-load and mod skills are not preserved; <Skill>Value getters call GetSkillValue which Debug.LogWarnings on a miss) is out of scope here but directly affects the plan's XSkillValue getters — need the Harmony-guard + per-city re-inject plan from the skill-focused task.

Whether ReorderableList / *PlanListEntry / NoManagerAssignedPopUp / *PlanUI prefabs are reachable at runtime via Resources or addressables for cloning, or truly require a shipped AssetBundle for a native-looking tab.

Exact semantics of EmployeeInstance.IsEmployeeAvailable() / IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() used to gate the native drivers (LogisticsManagerPlan.GetPlannedDeliveries) — the mod driver should replicate the same availability gating so a sick/absent/unscheduled manager stops supervision.
